Django

Django is a powerful Python web framework used to build secure, scalable, and high-performance web applications. It includes features such as an ORM, authentication system, admin panel, URL routing, templates, and REST API support for rapid development.

Learn Django fundamentals, models, views, templates, authentication, database integration, REST APIs, deployment, and best practices for professional web development.

Topics Covered

Django • Python • ORM • Templates • Authentication • REST API • PostgreSQL • MySQL • Deployment • Web Development

Why Django Is Useful for Production Backends

Django is designed around batteries-included development. Its ORM, migrations, authentication, forms, security defaults and admin interface let teams build complete business applications without assembling every feature from separate packages. That makes it a strong fit for dashboards, internal tools, content systems and API-backed web products.

A good Django learning project should cover models, relationships, validation, permissions and deployment rather than only URL routing. As applications grow, developers should also learn query optimization, caching, background jobs, static/media storage and production settings. Django REST Framework is commonly added when the same backend needs to serve mobile apps or JavaScript frontends.

Django for applications that need structure from the start

Django includes routing, templates, an ORM, authentication and an admin interface, which makes it a strong option for data-heavy business applications. The framework is opinionated enough to encourage consistent project structure while still allowing custom workflows.

Good Django engineering goes beyond models and views. Production systems also need permissions, migrations, validation, database indexes, secure settings, logging, backups and a deployment process that can be repeated safely.
